# `prefer-ends-with-scalar`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: idiomatic · Default: off · Fixes: fix all · Options: none

Reports calling `std.mem.endsWith` with a 1-character string literal (e.g.
`"/"`, `"."`, `"\n"`).
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

`std.mem.endsWith` slices the haystack and compares string slices through
`std.mem.eql`. Checking the final element directly via `slice.len > 0 and
slice[slice.len - 1] == 'c'` compiles to a single memory load and comparison
without function call or slice construction overhead.

## When it fires

```zig
// Inefficient: constructs slices and calls mem.eql
if (std.mem.endsWith(u8, path, "/")) { ... }

// Fast: single byte load and comparison
if (path.len > 0 and path[path.len - 1] == '/') { ... }
```

The rule reports only when the needle is a 1-character string literal.
Multi-character suffixes legitimately require string slice comparisons.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
const std = @import("std");

fn isDir(path: []const u8) bool {
    return std.mem.endsWith(u8, path, "/");
}
```
